story: As a visitor, I scroll the home page and see the five-act WebGL part story (hero, routed, glass box, assembly, $14.14 number, close) with captions fading in per section.
expected: Fixed WebGL PartStage renders behind content; a right-edge 6-stop progress rail (PART...PROOF) highlights the active act and clicking a dot scrolls to that section; a floating 'See it on your part' pill appears mid-story and links to /company#pilot; 'The full platform ->' links to /platform and 'or read the method first ->' links to /method. Page has no own metadata export, so tab title falls back to the (site) layout default 'ProofShape — verification, made of glass'.

story: As a visitor, I drag the quantity slider on the 'PROOF' act and watch the make-vs-tool-up recommendation flip at the 1,962-unit crossover.
expected: A range input (aria-label 'Quantity', log scale 1 to 10,000, default qty 500) updates the SVG curves, unit-cost readout, and highlighted curve; at qty <= 1962 the MJF 'make' branch is recommended, above it the injection-molding branch (qualified 'if redesigned'); an underline link below routes to /company#pilot.

story: As a visitor, I type my email in the close-act pill and click 'Request a pilot'.
expected: The email input is decorative — it is not inside a form and its value is never submitted or carried anywhere; 'Request a pilot' is a plain Link that navigates to /company#pilot regardless of input contents.

story: As a visitor on any marketing page, I use the top nav to reach every main section, log in, or request a pilot.
expected: Wordmark 'ProofShape' links to /; nav links Method, Platform, Teams, Security, Developers, Company route to those paths with the current section highlighted (data-active, including /teams/* subtree); 'Log in' -> /login; 'Request a pilot' -> /company#pilot. A mobile <details> menu mirrors all links, closes on link click and Escape. Cinematic pages use a transparent fixed variant, document pages a sticky blurred bar.

story: As a visitor, I use the footer to cross-navigate and reach legal pages.
expected: Footer shows tagline 'ProofShape — verification, made of glass', links Home + the six nav items + Log in, and a legal row with current year plus Privacy -> /privacy, Terms -> /terms, DPA -> /dpa, Status -> /status. Cinematic pages instead close with an inline tagline linking Method, Platform, Security, Developers.

story: As a visitor, I read how the $14.14 number is built: five-stage walk, scroll-assembled driver sum, honesty rail, and the +/-40% objection section.
expected: Document page in SiteShell; scrolling the record-assembly section reveals four drivers that reconcile to $14.14; closing CTAs 'Cost a part' -> /signup and 'Explore the platform' -> /platform. No page-level metadata export (title falls back to the layout default).

story: As a visitor, I read the platform overview (one engine, three surfaces) and continue to signup or the method.
expected: Static server-rendered page with metadata title 'Platform — ProofShape'; closing CTAs 'Cost a part' -> /signup and 'How the number is built' -> /method; nav/footer chrome via SiteShell.

story: As a visitor, I browse the five persona journeys and open the one matching my role.
expected: Metadata title 'Teams — ProofShape'; journey links route to /teams/in-house-manufacturing, /teams/cost-engineering, /teams/sourcing, /teams/design-engineering, /teams/shop-owners; closing CTAs 'Request a pilot' -> /company#pilot and 'Explore the platform' -> /platform.

story: As a cost engineer visitor, I scroll the cinematic journey and reach the pilot CTA.
expected: Server wrapper exports metadata 'For Cost Engineering — ProofShape' and renders the client cinematic (WebGL + scroll acts); an inline link back to /teams in the hero; closing CTAs are plain <a> tags to /company#pilot (solid) and /teams (ghost).

story: As a design engineer visitor, I scroll the five-act journey (flag, dial, fix, gate) and reach the pilot CTA.
expected: Client page ('use client', no metadata export — title falls back to layout default); scroll-driven caption reveals with no form/slider inputs; hero links back to /teams; closing CTAs Link to /company#pilot and /teams.

story: As a manufacturing/MRO visitor, I read the persona page and reach the pilot CTA.
expected: Server component with metadata 'ProofShape — For In-house manufacturing & MRO'; link back to /teams near the top; closing CTAs -> /company#pilot and /teams.

story: As a shop owner visitor, I scroll the cinematic journey and reach the pilot CTA.
expected: Server wrapper exports metadata 'For shop owners — ProofShape' and renders the client body; hero links back to /teams; closing CTAs -> /company#pilot and /teams.

story: As a sourcing/procurement visitor, I scroll the cinematic journey and reach the pilot CTA.
expected: Server wrapper exports metadata 'For Sourcing — ProofShape'; client SourcingView renders WebGL stage and scroll reveals; hero links back to /teams; closing CTAs -> /company#pilot (PILOT_HREF) and /teams.

story: As a developer visitor, I read the API pitch with the fixture JSON record reveal and continue to signup or docs.
expected: Static server page with metadata 'Developers — ProofShape'; the JSON 'record arriving' reveal is pure CSS (no client JS); closing CTAs 'Get an API key' -> /signup and 'Full API reference' -> /docs.

story: As a developer visitor, I land on the durable API reference doorway and jump to the interactive console.
expected: Metadata 'API Reference - ProofShape'; 'Open API console' is an <a> to /scalar and 'Developer overview' links to /developers; a static <pre> lists the four endpoints (POST /api/v1/validate, POST /api/v1/validate/cost, GET /api/v1/cost-decisions, GET /api/v1/catalog) with Bearer auth note.

story: As a visitor, I read the mission, the four-week pilot program, why-now, and contact sections, arriving at #pilot from any 'Request a pilot' CTA.
expected: Metadata 'Company — ProofShape'; section id='pilot' has scrollMarginTop so /company#pilot lands below the sticky nav; four WeekCell columns describe the pilot; contact section points to the form (no email address published); chrome via SiteShell.

story: As a prospective customer, I submit the pilot request form (work email, company, what you make, deployment preference) and receive a durable receipt.
expected: On mount the form GETs /api/pilot/request for a Turnstile site key (submit disabled until ready, and until the Turnstile token exists when a key is configured); submit POSTs JSON {requestId (UUID, reused for retry idempotency), email, company, what, deployment, turnstileToken, website honeypot} to /api/pilot/request, which validates and forwards to the backend /auth/pilot-request; success replaces the form with a 'Request received' status showing receipt 'CV-<id>'; failures show role=alert error text and reset Turnstile. Required-field validation on email/company/what; deployment select offers undecided/cloud/vpc/air-gapped.

story: As a security reviewer visitor, I read the deployment models (cloud, self-hosted, air-gapped) and data-handling claims.
expected: Metadata 'Security — ProofShape'; no compliance badges; closing CTAs 'Talk to us' -> /company#pilot and 'Self-host it today' -> /developers; chrome via SiteShell.

story: As a visitor evaluating a pilot, I read what the closeout report contains (held-out accuracy, floor declaration, decision ledger, next actions).
expected: Metadata 'Pilot Report - ProofShape'; four numbered cards render from a static list; single CTA 'Request a pilot' -> /company#pilot; chrome via SiteShell.

story: As a visitor, I read how CAD, account, pilot, and usage data are handled.
expected: Metadata 'Privacy - ProofShape'; sections What we collect / How it is used / Retention and deletion; 'Talk to ProofShape' pill links to /company#pilot; also linked from the pilot form's fallback note.

story: As a visitor, I read the public service terms (evidence-not-authority framing, accounts, uploads, pilot terms).
expected: Metadata 'Terms - ProofShape'; static article, no links or CTAs beyond shared nav/footer; reachable from the footer legal row.

story: As a procurement/security visitor, I read DPA availability, subprocessors, and security-review process.
expected: Metadata 'Data Processing Addendum - ProofShape'; static article stating the DPA travels with the pilot and questionnaires go through pilot intake; no form or CTA links in body.

story: As a visitor, I check service status and see an explicit statement that no public feed exists yet rather than synthetic uptime.
expected: Metadata 'Status - ProofShape'; three rows (Hosted app, API, Workers) each read 'No public metric feed yet'; no fake green indicators; linked from the footer legal row.

story: As a visitor hitting a bad or private link, I see a branded 404 inside the site chrome and can return home.
expected: not-found.tsx renders inside SiteShell with heading 'That record is not here.' and a 'Back to ProofShape' pill linking to /; nav and footer remain fully functional.

story: As a visitor when a page crashes, I see a generic error screen with an error ID and can retry.
expected: Root error boundary captures the exception to Sentry with the digest, shows 'Something went wrong', renders 'Error ID: <digest>' when present, and a 'Try again' button that calls the retry callback to re-render. Note: it uses product UI (Button, light tokens), not the site-theater chrome.

story: As a crawler (or SEO auditor), I fetch robots.txt and sitemap.xml and get the correct public-route inventory.
expected: robots.txt allows the 18 public marketing routes and disallows app/auth routes (/analyze, /verify, /login, /signup, /settings, etc.), pointing at ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL}/sitemap.xml; sitemap.xml lists the same 18 routes with priority 1.0 for home and 0.7 elsewhere; a root opengraph-image.tsx serves the social preview image and the (site) layout supplies the default title/description.
